definitions.rationale: This macro equation expands bfBody into the exact MPY statement term for the submitted function, so it defines a named program term rather than adding an execution or mathematical fact.
definitions.text:
rule bfBody =>
    Assign(
      Name("planets"),
      TupleExpr(
        Str("Mercury"),
        Str("Venus"),
        Str("Earth"),
        Str("Mars"),
        Str("Jupiter"),
        Str("Saturn"),
        Str("Uranus"),
        Str("Neptune")))
    If(
      BoolOp(
        "or",
        Compare(Name("planet1"), CmpOp("not in", Name("planets"))),
        Compare(Name("planet2"), CmpOp("not in", Name("planets")))),
      Return(TupleExpr(.Exprs)),
      .Stmts)
    Assign(
      Name("index1"),
      Call(Attribute(Name("planets"), "index"), Name("planet1")))
    Assign(
      Name("index2"),
      Call(Attribute(Name("planets"), "index"), Name("planet2")))
    If(
      Compare(Name("index1"), CmpOp("<", Name("index2"))),
      Return(
        Subscript(
          Name("planets"),
          Slice(
            BinOp("+", Name("index1"), Int(1)),
            Name("index2"),
            NoBound))),
      .Stmts)
    Return(
      Subscript(
        Name("planets"),
        Slice(
          BinOp("+", Name("index2"), Int(1)),
          Name("index1"),
          NoBound)))

definitions.rationale: This macro equation expands bfModule into the module containing the bf definition and therefore is a structural definition of a named proof term.
This macro equation expands bfCall into the ordinary MPY Call term with two string arguments, defining entry syntax without replacing call execution.
definitions.text:
rule bfCall(P1, P2) =>
    Call(Name("bf"), str(P1), str(P2))

definitions.rationale: This equation defines planetValues as the fixed ordered eight-element planet sequence used by the mathematical postcondition.
definitions.text:
rule planetValues =>
    vCons(str(strToCodes("Mercury")),
    vCons(str(strToCodes("Venus")),
    vCons(str(strToCodes("Earth")),
    vCons(str(strToCodes("Mars")),
    vCons(str(strToCodes("Jupiter")),
    vCons(str(strToCodes("Saturn")),
    vCons(str(strToCodes("Uranus")),
    vCons(str(strToCodes("Neptune")), .ValSeq))))))))

definitions.rationale: This guarded equation is the Mercury case of the total planetIndex definition, assigning index 0 exactly when the input code sequence is Mercury.
This guarded equation is the Venus case of the total planetIndex definition, assigning index 1 exactly when the input code sequence is Venus.
This guarded equation is the Earth case of the total planetIndex definition, assigning index 2 exactly when the input code sequence is Earth.
This guarded equation is the Mars case of the total planetIndex definition, assigning index 3 exactly when the input code sequence is Mars.
This guarded equation is the Jupiter case of the total planetIndex definition, assigning index 4 exactly when the input code sequence is Jupiter.
This guarded equation is the Saturn case of the total planetIndex definition, assigning index 5 exactly when the input code sequence is Saturn.
This guarded equation is the Uranus case of the total planetIndex definition, assigning index 6 exactly when the input code sequence is Uranus.
This guarded equation is the Neptune case of the total planetIndex definition, assigning index 7 exactly when the input code sequence is Neptune.
This complementary guarded equation completes the planetIndex definition by assigning -1 exactly when the input differs from all eight planet names.
definitions.text:
rule planetIndex(P) => -1
    requires notBool (P ==K strToCodes("Mercury"))
     andBool notBool (P ==K strToCodes("Venus"))
     andBool notBool (P ==K strToCodes("Earth"))
     andBool notBool (P ==K strToCodes("Mars"))
     andBool notBool (P ==K strToCodes("Jupiter"))
     andBool notBool (P ==K strToCodes("Saturn"))
     andBool notBool (P ==K strToCodes("Uranus"))
     andBool notBool (P ==K strToCodes("Neptune"))

definitions.rationale: This equation defines betweenPlanets compositionally by applying the planetIndex definition to both inputs and passing the indices to betweenIndices.
This guarded equation defines the invalid-index case of betweenIndices as the empty value sequence whenever either index is negative.
definitions.text:
rule betweenIndices(I, J) => .ValSeq
    requires I <Int 0 orBool J <Int 0

definitions.rationale: This guarded equation defines the ascending-index case of betweenIndices as the slice strictly after I and before J.
definitions.text:
rule betweenIndices(I, J) => buildVS(planetValues, I +Int 1, J, 1)
    requires I >=Int 0 andBool J >=Int 0 andBool I <Int J

definitions.rationale: This guarded equation defines the reverse-or-equal-index case of betweenIndices as the slice strictly after J and before I.
definitions.text:
rule betweenIndices(I, J) => buildVS(planetValues, J +Int 1, I, 1)
    requires I >=Int 0 andBool J >=Int 0 andBool I >=Int J
